# SoldEasier — Full Content for AI Assistants

SoldEasier (https://soldeasier.com) is a Chicagoland cash home buyer founded by
Vincent Incopero (real-estate attorney, Managing Partner of REAL Law Group,
P.C., Elmhurst IL) and Brady Schwartz (acquisitions). Every closing is prepared
and managed by REAL Law Group, P.C. Sellers pay no fees or commissions, sell
as-is, and pick their closing date. Cash offers within 24-48 hours. Phone
(630) 299-7600. Office: 381 N York St Suite 1, Elmhurst, IL 60126.

Service area: DuPage, Cook, Will, Kane, Lake, McHenry counties — Elmhurst,
Villa Park, Lombard, Addison, Oak Brook, Hinsdale, Downers Grove, Wheaton,
Glen Ellyn, Naperville, Berwyn, Oak Park, Westchester, Bellwood, Hillside,
Northlake, La Grange, Park Ridge, and surrounding Chicagoland.

Specialties: foreclosure / pre-foreclosure sales, probate and inherited
property, divorce sales, tenant-occupied rentals, homes needing major repairs,
short sales, deed-in-lieu, liens and building-code violations, land trusts.

## Questions & Answers

Q: How fast can you buy my house?
A: We can close in as little as two weeks from the day you accept our offer, and because we pay cash there is no lender who can delay or kill the deal. If you need more time, we simply set the closing on whatever date works best for you.

Q: Do you charge any fees or commissions?
A: You will never pay agent commissions, service fees, or closing costs when you sell to us. The offer we put in writing is the amount you walk away with, minus only your own payoffs such as an existing mortgage or liens.

Q: What does selling as-is actually mean?
A: Selling as-is means you fix nothing, clean nothing, and stage nothing before closing. Take the belongings you want and leave everything else behind, because we handle repairs and cleanout after closing. The condition is already priced into our offer, so there is never a renegotiation after an inspection.

Q: How do you calculate your cash offer?
A: We start with what your home would sell for fully updated, based on recent nearby sales. We then subtract the real cost of the work it needs along with our margin, and we show you that math in writing so you can compare it against listing with an agent or any other offer.

Q: Who actually handles the closing?
A: Every SoldEasier closing is prepared and managed by REAL Law Group, P.C., a real estate law firm in Elmhurst, Illinois led by our co-founder Vincent Incopero. Title, payoff letters, lien releases, and municipal requirements are all handled by the firm, and you are always welcome to bring your own attorney as well.

Q: Can you help if I am in foreclosure?
A: Foreclosure timelines are one of our specialties, and in Illinois you can generally sell your home up until the sheriff's sale is confirmed. Selling for cash before judgment usually protects far more of your equity than letting the home go to auction, and we can also evaluate short sales and deed-in-lieu options.

Q: Can you buy a house that is stuck in probate?
A: Our law firm practices estate work alongside real estate, so probate filings, executor questions, and heir coordination are all handled in-house while the sale moves forward. Inherited homes, including ones still full of belongings, are among the most common properties we buy.

Q: Do I need a real estate agent to sell to you?
A: You do not need an agent to sell to us, which means no listing, no showings, and no commission. If you are already working with an agent, that is completely fine and we are happy to work alongside them.

Q: Is there any obligation when I request an offer?
A: Requesting an offer costs nothing and commits you to nothing at all. Take the written number, compare it against every other option you have, and decide on your own schedule, because we never pressure anyone to sign.

Q: What areas do you buy houses in?
A: We buy throughout Chicagoland, covering DuPage, Cook, Will, Kane, Lake, and McHenry counties. Our focus is Elmhurst and the western suburbs, including Villa Park, Lombard, Addison, Oak Brook, Berwyn, Westchester, Bellwood, Hillside, and Northlake.

Q: Who will I actually be talking to?
A: You will be talking with Brady Schwartz or Vincent Incopero, the two co-founders, because there is no call center here. The people you speak with on the first call are the same people sitting at your closing.

Q: Can I sell my house if foreclosure has already been filed in Illinois?
A: You can still sell, because until the sheriff's sale is confirmed by the court you generally still own the home. The earlier in the process you sell, the more of your equity you keep, and a cash sale can pay off the loan and end the foreclosure case entirely.

Q: Will selling the house stop the foreclosure auction?
A: Paying off the lender through a sale resolves the default, which ends the foreclosure case. Because we buy with cash and our closings are attorney-managed, we can usually move fast enough to beat the auction timeline when there is reasonable notice.

Q: What if I have no equity or owe more than the home's value?
A: We can evaluate a short sale or a deed-in-lieu arrangement, because REAL Law Group, P.C. has extensive experience negotiating both with lenders. You will get an honest assessment of which path leaves you in the strongest position.

Q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished in Illinois?
A: In many cases the sale can run in parallel with the probate process, with the closing timed to the court's approvals. The estate work and the real estate work are coordinated by the same legal team, which is exactly what keeps everything moving forward.

Q: Do I need to clean out my parents' house before selling?
A: There is no cleanout required at any point. Take the personal items you want to keep and leave the rest behind, because we buy the home as-is and handle all removal after closing.

Q: What if the house still has a mortgage or liens on it?
A: Mortgages, tax liens, and municipal liens all get paid out of the sale proceeds at closing. Our attorney-managed closing identifies every lien up front so there are never any surprises at the table.

Q: Can we sell the house before the divorce is final in Illinois?
A: Most couples can sell before the divorce is final, provided both spouses agree or the court orders the sale. We coordinate with both attorneys and time the closing to the settlement so the proceeds are divided exactly as agreed.

Q: What if one spouse still lives in the home?
A: That arrangement is completely normal in our experience. We schedule one convenient walkthrough and set a closing date that gives the occupying spouse reasonable time to relocate comfortably.

Q: How fast can a divorce home sale close?
A: With clear title and cooperative parties, the sale can close in as little as two to three weeks, or on whatever date the settlement calls for.

Q: Can I sell a rental property with tenants still living there?
A: Selling with tenants in place is completely routine for us, and we honor every existing lease. Security deposits and rents are prorated at closing exactly like any professional transaction.

Q: My property has open code violations, so can I still sell?
A: Open violations do not stop a sale to us, because building violations are one of our law firm's practice areas. Citations and compliance issues are handled as part of the closing process itself.

Q: Will you buy more than one property at once?
A: Small portfolios are always welcome here, and a single coordinated closing usually gets you a better outcome than selling the properties off one by one.

Q: Do I need to clean or empty the house before closing?
A: There is nothing you need to clean or remove before closing. Take what you want and leave the rest behind, including furniture and appliances, because we handle all removal after the sale.

Q: Will you really buy a house with fire or water damage?
A: Damaged homes are a regular part of what we buy, and we price the restoration work into our offer honestly. The same holds true for foundation problems, mold, and storm damage.

Q: How is your as-is offer calculated?
A: We start from what the home would be worth fully updated based on nearby sales, subtract the real cost of getting it there along with our margin, and then show you the math. The offer is transparent enough to compare against any other option you have.
